title: Incident Execution Guide, Runbooks, and Communication Templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This page is an operational playbook for executing incidents from detection through postmortem and remediation. It standardizes roles, runbook structure, alert thresholds, communication templates, rotation rules, and game day exercises. Use this guide as the canonical source for incident execution across Redwood Inference services.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted and Dedicated/Private control-plane services that impact customer-facing inference APIs, console, or billing.
- Excludes routine CI failures and development branch problems (handled by triage owners).

Key definitions:
- Incident: any event causing customer-visible degradation or data/control plane impact for >30s or impacting >0.5% of requests in a region for >5 minutes.
- Severity levels: P0 (system down or data loss), P1 (significant customer impact), P2 (degraded performance impacting SLAs), P3 (minor or isolated issues).

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detection & Alerting
   - Sources: Prometheus alerts, tracing-based anomaly detectors, Synthetics (every region), customer-reported tickets, platform health probes.
   - Automatic triage: Alerts with matching runbook tags are routed to oncall via PagerDuty with escalation policies defined below.
2) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   - Pager acknowledges, documents initial symptoms in the incident channel (Slack #inc-<service>-<region>).
   - If impact meets P1/P0 criteria, auto-page Incident Commander (IC) and notify Product/Customer Success.
3) Containment & Mitigation
   - IC assigns roles and calls for mitigation steps. Mitigation goal: stop customer impact, minimize blast radius, restore availability.
4) Restoration
   - Validate service health across regions, update status page, and begin traffic rehoming if required.
5) Post-incident review
   - Capture timeline within 48 hours; full postmortem completed in 7 business days with action items and owners.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): Leads incident, sets priorities, owns the incident timeline, and makes rollout/fallback decisions. (Default: SRE oncall lead).
- Communications Lead: Owns customer-facing comms, status page updates, internal summaries. (Default: oncall primary until handed to PM/CS).
- Engineering Owner(s): Service-owner engineers who run remediation steps and confirm fixes.
- Support Liaison: Triage customer tickets, surfaces relevant customer impact details.
- War Room Coordinator: Creates and moderates incident Slack channel, ensures notes and recordings are captured.

On-call rotations and handoffs:
- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary oncall for SREs, 1 week secondary. Follow policy: maximum 6 consecutive weeks oncall per year per engineer.
- Handoff checklist (to run at every rotation swap):
  1. Confirm PagerDuty schedule and escalation contacts.
  2. Confirm access (kube, cloud console, logs-bucket).
  3. Review 3 most recent active runbooks and ongoing incidents.
  4. Share any planned maintenance windows.
- Handoff message example:
  "Handoff: @alice -> @bob. Primary oncall for inference-core this week. No active incidents. Known maintenance: database patch Thursday 02:00 UTC. Key dashboards: /dashboards/inference-overview. PD escalation: pd://redwood/inference-primary.

Runbook structure (required fields):
- Title (service-region-tag)
- Purpose and scope
- Owner & reviewers (team email + schedule)
- Triggers (alerts / symptoms that should cause invocation)
- Pre-flight checks (e.g., verify region, check KV cache status)
- Step-by-step mitigation (numbered, idempotent steps)
- Validation (how to confirm success)
- Rollback / fallback plan
- Post-incident tasks & references

Sample runbook (truncated):
---
Title: inference-api-high-5xx-us-east-1
Owner: inference-svc-team@redwood.com
Triggers:
- prometheus: inference_api_5xx_rate > 0.5% (5m)
- synthetic: /health returns 500 from 3 probes in 2 regions
Steps:
1) Confirm the alert: grep "5xx" /var/logs/inference/* | tail -n 200
2) Check deployment health: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | egrep "CrashLoop|0/"
3) If new deploy in last 30m: rollback: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=<previous>
4) If not deploy-related: scale down suspect node pool: gcloud container clusters resize <cluster> --node-pool=<pool> --num-nodes=<reduced>
5) Purge local KV caches on affected hosts: redis-cli -h <host> FLUSHDB (only if cached keys are ephemeral)
Validation:
- requests_p95 latency returns below 400ms across 5 minutes
- 5xx rate < 0.1% for 10 consecutive minutes
---

Alert thresholds and metric guidelines (examples):
- 5xx error rate: trigger if >0.5% requests for 5m (P1), >2.0% for 2m (P0).
- Latency: p95 > 1000ms for 5m -> investigate P1. p99 > 2s for 3m -> P0.
- Queue backpressure: queued requests > 5k in a region -> P1.
- Synthetic failures: 3 region probes failing in 5m -> P1.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Primary oncall (first 5 minutes)
- After 5 minutes with unresolved mitigation: escalate to secondary oncall + IC auto-notify
- After 15 minutes for P0 events: page Engineering Director + Head of SRE + Customer Success lead

Status page and customer comms templates:
- Use status.redwood.ai for public status. For Dedicated/Private customers also use ticketing system and account-level email templates.

Templates (copy/paste and fill placeholders)
1) Initial acknowledgement (15 minutes):
Subject: [Incident] Redwood Inference – {service} experiencing errors in {region}
Body:
Hello,
We are aware of elevated errors impacting {service} in {region}. Our oncall team is investigating.
Impact: {brief sentence on scope e.g., 20% of requests returning 5xx}
What we are doing: Establishing mitigation, routing traffic, and rolling back suspect deployments.
Next update: within 30 minutes or sooner.
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/{incident-id}
Contact: support@redwood.ai
2) Ongoing update (every 30 minutes):
Subject: [Update] Incident {incident-id}: {service} in {region}
Body:
Update at {time UTC}:
- What changed since last update: {progress summary}
- Current impact: {customers/regions affected and percent of traffic}
- Actions taken: {actions}
- Next steps & ETA: {next steps}
3) Resolution notice:
Subject: [Resolved] Incident {incident-id}: {service} in {region}
Body:
The incident impacting {service} in {region} is resolved as of {time UTC}.
Impact summary: {duration, affected customers, root cause (initial)}
Follow-up: A full post-incident review will be published when complete with action items and timelines.
Contact: support@redwood.ai

Customer status page content guidelines:
- Keep language non-technical and candid.
- Include impact, work underway, ETA (if available), and mitigation steps.
- Mark updates with timestamps and an internal incident id.
- For sensitive incidents (data loss, security), route updates through Security & Legal for approval.

Post-incident review process:
- Draft timeline (owner: IC) due within 48 hours — includes minute-level timeline, alerts, and remediation steps taken.
- Full postmortem document due within 7 business days. Postmortem must include: summary, timeline, root cause analysis (5 whys / RCA), corrective actions (owner and ETA), and verification plan.
- Postmortem review: mandatory review meeting attended by IC, owners, SRE manager, and PM.
- Action tracking: add all remediation tasks to the incident JIRA/project board with labels: incident-<id>, postmortem, blocker. Owners must provide progress updates weekly until complete.

Game day program (recommended cadence):
- Quarterly regional failover exercise (target: rotate primary traffic across regions without customer downtime).
- Monthly mini-simulations: single-service degradation with 30-minute time-boxed resolution.
- Annual full-stack P0 simulation conducted with exec observers.
Game day outputs:
- Runbook gaps report, playbook updates, training assignments.
- Scorecard: average MTTR, missed steps, communication quality (customer-facing clarity).

Runbook maintenance & governance:
- Ownership: every runbook must list an owner and two reviewers. Runbooks are reviewed quarterly.
- Retirement: deprecated runbooks archived with reason and date.
- PR process: runbook edits are submitted via docs repo PR; urgency edits allowed with follow-up review within 5 business days.

Oncall wellbeing and limits:
- Block high-stress sequences: restrict scheduled changes during primary oncall week unless emergency.
- Offer 4 hours backup time after P0 events for rest & paperwork (approved by manager).

Appendices:
- Useful CLI snippets:
  - View recent deploys: kubectl -n inference rollout history deployment/inference-api
  - Force rollback: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=<rev>
  - Query error rate: prometheus-query 'sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",job="inference"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference"}[5m]))'

- Example incident timeline (abbreviated):
  00:00 Alert fires: 5xx rate spike detected (0.8%)
  00:02 PagerDuty acknowledged by oncall
  00:06 Triage finds suspect deploy 00:45 UTC -> rollback initiated 00:07
  00:14 Error rate begins to decline -> p95 latency improving
  00:20 Traffic normalized; status page updated to "Partial degradations being mitigated"
  01:10 Incident declared resolved; IC closes incident and assigns postmortem owner

- Postmortem template header (to copy into PRD):
  Title: {incident-id} – {short summary}
  Severity: {P0/P1/P2}
  Timeline owner: {name}
  Root cause: {summary}
  Corrective actions: - {action} (owner, ETA)

Contact matrix & escalation contacts (always keep PD entries up to date):
- SRE primary: oncall-sre-primary@redwood.ai
- Engineering director: director-eng@redwood.ai
- CS incident liaison: cs-liaison@redwood.ai
